subject: Allometry: Visually significant predlines and insignificant pairwise tests.

messages.subject: Allometry: Visually significant predlines and insignificant pairwise tests.
parts:
Dear everyone,

I am having some issues understanding the results from my pairwise after carrying out an allometry analysis.

I read a couple of threads on the topic in this group and below is an answer that may make sense. Although, my sample size seems reasonable in my case. Therefore, I wonder if it is the way I use my codes which may cause these results. I am new to this kind of analysis and codes can be hard to understand. I would greatly appreciate it if somebody with a greater understanding than mine could help me understand these results 😊

A previous answer to this question:

„First, it is possible that one has a significant linear model effect with no pairwise comparisons being significant. This can occur in univariate anova-type models as well as multivariate models. Usually this boils down to power and sample size: in the aggregate there is enough signal to detect an effect, but broken down by pairs there is insufficient power to identify this (the alternative; a significant pairwise but not full anova is also possible, but for slightly different reasons).”

My codes:

### GDF with removed offshore and Unknown ###

# indices, tells which individuals to remove #

indices <- tursiopsBending.dt$spec$Sex != "Unknown" & tursiopsBending.dt$spec$State3 != "Offshore"

# Subset the array "tursiopsbending_sym.dt$symm.sh" along the third dimension using the indices. The third dimension represents the individuals #

tursiopsBending.dt$gpa.sh <- tursiopsBending.dt$gpa.sh[, , indices, drop = FALSE]

# Subset the individuals along "tursiopsbending_sym.dt$cs" #

tursiopsBending.dt$cs <- tursiopsBending.dt$cs[indices, drop = FALSE]

# Prepare the sex, ecotype and individual variables removing the unwanted individuals #

filtered_spec <- tursiopsBending.dt$spec[tursiopsBending.dt$spec$Sex != "Unknown" & tursiopsBending.dt$spec$State3 != "Offshore", ]

tursiopsBending.dt$spec <- filtered_spec

 # Produce the gdf #

gdf <- geomorph.data.frame(shape = tursiopsBending.dt$gpa.sh, sex = tursiopsBending.dt$spec$Sex, ind = tursiopsBending.dt$spec$LabID, Csize=tursiopsBending.dt$cs)

attributes(gdf)

### Allometry test on Sex only ###

fit.unique.Sex <- procD.lm(shape ~ log(Csize) * sex, data = gdf, iter = 9999) #unique

# Plot Predline #

plotAllometry(fit.unique.Sex, size = gdf$Csize, logsz = TRUE, method = "PredLine", pch = 19, col = color)

# Pairwise #

PW.allo.sex <-pairwise(fit.unique.Sex, groups = gdf$sex, covariate = log(gdf$Csize))

My results :

 Kind regards, 

Morgane
